question: What is the primary function of an Automated External Defibrillator?

options.A: Monitoring blood pressure and oxygen saturation levels continuously
options.B: Delivering a shock to restart a stopped heart
options.C: Analyzing heart rhythms and delivering a shock when needed
options.D: Providing mechanical chest compressions during cardiac arrest

explanation: An AED is specifically designed to read heart rhythms and automatically determine if an electrical shock is required. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T3#GNS315_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why is early defibrillation vital for a patient in sudden cardiac arrest?

options.A: Survival chances drop rapidly with every passing minute
options.B: It prevents the lungs from filling up with fluid
options.C: Late shocks cause permanent damage to the brain stem
options.D: It immediately restores normal breathing patterns without CPR

explanation: Delaying defibrillation allows the heart muscle to weaken further, drastically reducing the likelihood of successful resuscitation. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T3#GNS315_U4_T3_h1)

question: Which clinical sign must be present before applying an AED?

options.A: Dizziness and pale, sweaty skin tone
options.B: Severe chest pain radiating to the left arm
options.C: Unresponsiveness and absence of normal breathing
options.D: High blood pressure and a racing pulse

explanation: An AED is indicated when a patient is unresponsive and not breathing normally, signaling cardiac arrest. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T3#GNS315_U4_T3_h2)

question: A patient is gasping irregularly and cannot be woken up. What should you do?

options.A: Treat the gasping as normal breathing and monitor
options.B: Wait ten minutes to see if regular breathing returns
options.C: Assume cardiac arrest and prepare the AED immediately
options.D: Place the patient in the recovery position right away

explanation: Agonal gasps are not normal breathing and often occur during cardiac arrest, requiring immediate resuscitation efforts. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T3#GNS315_U4_T3_h2)

question: Which heart rhythm is classified as shockable by an AED?
explanation: Ventricular Fibrillation is a chaotic, shockable rhythm where the heart fails to pump blood effectively. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T3#GNS315_U4_T3_h3)

question: What happens inside the heart during Ventricular Tachycardia without a pulse?

options.A: Blood flows backward from the aorta into the lungs
options.B: The atria contract faster than the ventricles can relax
options.C: The heart beats too fast to fill with blood
options.D: The heart stops all electrical activity completely

explanation: Rapid ventricular contractions prevent adequate filling time, causing a drastic drop in blood flow and a lack of pulse. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T3#GNS315_U4_T3_h3)

question: Where should the upper right AED pad be placed on the chest?

options.A: In the center of the sternum
options.B: On the upper left back region

explanation: The standard anterior-lateral placement requires the first pad on the upper right chest below the clavicle. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T3#GNS315_U4_T3_h4)

question: A patient has a very hairy chest preventing the AED pads from sticking. What is the best action?

options.A: Apply extra gel and press the pads down firmly over the hair
options.B: Skip using the AED and continue chest compressions only
options.C: Place the pads directly over a heavy winter vest instead
options.D: Shave the hair quickly using the razor in the AED kit

explanation: Excessive chest hair prevents proper pad adhesion and electrical contact, so it must be removed rapidly. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T3#GNS315_U4_T3_h4)

question: When is the best time to resume chest compressions after an AED shock?

options.A: After waiting for two full minutes of rest
options.B: When the device finishes analyzing a second time
options.C: Only when the patient starts coughing loudly

explanation: Resuming chest compressions right after a shock helps maintain blood flow without unnecessary delay. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T3#GNS315_U4_T3_h5)

question: What must rescuers do while the AED is analyzing the heart rhythm?

options.A: Check the patient's pupils for a light reflex
options.B: Stop chest compressions and stay clear of the patient
options.C: Ventilate the lungs using a bag-valve-mask device
options.D: Continue performing fast chest compressions uninterrupted

explanation: Motion from rescuers or CPR can interfere with the AED's ability to accurately read the heart rhythm. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T3#GNS315_U4_T3_h5)

question: What should a nurse do if a patient has an implanted pacemaker visible on the chest?

options.A: Avoid using the AED entirely under any circumstances
options.B: Disconnect the pacemaker wires before turning on the AED
options.C: Place the AED pad directly on top of the pacemaker metal
options.D: Place the AED pad at least one inch away from the device

explanation: Placing pads directly over an implanted device can block energy transfer, so offset the pad slightly. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T3#GNS315_U4_T3_h6)

question: Why is it necessary to dry a patient's chest before applying AED pads?

options.A: To help the adhesive glue stick securely to the oily skin
options.B: To prevent the electrical current from short-circuiting across the skin
options.C: To ensure the ECG leads pick up respiratory movements
options.D: To lower the body temperature of the febrile patient

explanation: Excess moisture on the skin can cause the electrical shock to travel across the surface rather than through the heart. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T3#GNS315_U4_T3_h6)

question: Why is the recovery position recommended for an unconscious patient who regains a pulse?

options.A: To make it easier to attach more AED pads
options.B: To lower the blood pressure in the brain
options.C: To keep the chest muscles relaxed and warm
options.D: To prevent the tongue from blocking the airway

explanation: The recovery position keeps the airway open and allows fluids or vomit to drain safely out of the mouth. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T3#GNS315_U4_T3_h7)

question: Which detail is most important to communicate during a post-resuscitation handover?

options.A: The exact brand name of the AED device used
options.B: The name of the family member who found the patient
options.C: The hospital room number where the incident occurred
options.D: Total number of shocks delivered by the AED

explanation: The receiving medical team needs to know the resuscitation timeline and interventions performed to guide ongoing care. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T3#GNS315_U4_T3_h7)

question: How do most modern AEDs indicate that they are functional and ready for use?

options.A: By flashing a status indicator light or blinking icon
options.B: By sounding a loud continuous alarm every morning
options.C: By sending an email notification to the biomedical department
options.D: By printing out a weekly diagnostic report automatically

explanation: Most AEDs perform routine internal self-tests and display a visual status indicator to show readiness. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T3#GNS315_U4_T3_h8)

question: Why is routine inspection of AED electrode pads necessary during equipment checks?

options.A: The conductive gel on the pads can dry out over time
options.B: The adhesive loses its color after being stored in a box
options.C: The wires inside the pads rust when exposed to room air
options.D: Expired pads will cause the AED to deliver twice the normal voltage

explanation: If the gel dries out, the pads will fail to properly conduct the electrical shock to the patient's heart. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T3#GNS315_U4_T3_h8)
